sage-50.usage: Use for calm notes, selected states, and low-emphasis therapy scaffolding.

sage-500.usage: Use for primary CTAs, progress, and committed selection.

sage-700.usage: Use for tactile button depth, emphasized labels, and strong borders.

canvas.usage: Use as the quiet app canvas behind structured surfaces.

surface.usage: Use for inputs, cards, sheets, and main content panels.

ink.usage: Use for body copy, labels, headings, and validation text.

danger.usage: Use only for destructive actions or clear error feedback.

display.usage: Reflective completion headings and rare emotional emphasis.

body.usage: Main product copy and entered user text.

label.usage: Buttons, labels, validation, and compact instructions.

focus-glow.usage: Quiet focus ring for inputs and selectable controls.

cta-depth.usage: Physical rim for primary button press depth.

state-transition.usage: Use for state changes, reveals, disabled transitions, and validation.

press-feedback.usage: Use for button compression, chip selection, and tactile card taps.

motion.reducedMotion: Use opacity or instant state changes. Do not gate content on motion.

PrimaryButton.description: Sage fill, white label, deep sage rim, 56px default height, pill radius, tactile press state.

SecondaryButton.description: White surface, crisp border, ink label, and no decorative shadow.

TextInput.description: White writing surface with sage border, 20px radius, readable placeholder, and optional voice affordance.

GuidanceNote.description: Sage-tinted instructional box with concise copy and no assistant branding.

SuggestionRow.description: Optional starting point row with plain text and a compact Use action.

ValidationNote.description: Inline feedback that explains quality or readiness, not just length.

narrative.overview: A restrained CBT product UI where the user's own words lead and optional support stays secondary.
rules: Put the primary input before suggestions on vulnerable exercise steps.
Use AI suggestions as optional starting points, not the visual hero.
Use Cormorant for reflective hierarchy, never for controls.
Keep validation specific to task quality.
Require privacy-aware context for voice controls.
dos: Keep therapeutic copy short and concrete.
donts: Do not over-round cards or inputs.
Do not use sparkles or assistant decoration for suggestions.
Do not prime users with harsh thoughts before they write.
